observation.visible_scene: A linear-motion test rig viewed from a high angle: two long fixed wooden beams (one far/top, one near/bottom) each carry a horizontal polished metal rod. Four blue linear-bearing blocks ride on the rods (two per rod), and the blocks are tied to two wooden boards (a central board at the far rod and a near board at the near rod) that move as a carriage. A black metal frame with red adjustment knobs sits in the background. A person's hand(s) appear at the bottom edge of the frame.
visible_changes: The carriage (boards + all four bearing blocks) slides horizontally along the fixed rods: it drifts rightward to a rightmost position around the middle of the excerpt, then leftward to a leftmost position near the three-quarter mark, then begins moving rightward again by the last frame.

The far and near bearing blocks keep a roughly constant spacing to each other on their own rod while translating, consistent with one rigid carriage; the apparent left/right offset between the far pair and the near pair changes in a way consistent with perspective as the carriage moves across the frame.
The two long wooden beams, the two metal rods, and the background black frame remain stationary throughout, so the change is object motion, not camera motion (camera is essentially static).
A left hand with the index finger extended touches/hovers over the near-left bearing block at the start, then withdraws out of frame.
A right hand enters from the lower right, moves up, and rests on/around the near-right bearing block for a stretch, then leaves the frame.
The left hand re-enters later and hovers at/touches the near-left bearing block again toward the end.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the hands are driving the carriage or merely resting on it, and what produced the oscillation, is not shown.
The full travel range and the state of the rig before t=0 and after t=2.67 s are outside this crop.
Whether this is part of a longer demonstration sequence is unknown.
uncertain_details: The measured spacing of the two near-rod bearing blocks varies slightly across frames; this may be perspective distortion rather than real change, and cannot be confirmed as deformation.
Exact finger contact versus hovering near the bearing blocks is ambiguous in several frames.
The relative phase between the near and far pairs (rigid vs. independent) is inferred from consistent offsets plus perspective, not directly measured.
